answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, held in escrow until finality, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. A karst of per-task receipts records who did what, and the garden of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. What survives to the kernel is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short.
